Reading issueFilters lines 90-120.

actorEnvelope and resolveActorForOrg are one paragraph. issue.created is not subscribed. Creating an issue with an assignee does not emit issue.assigned. countIssues defaults to live scope. Archived issues are filtered out unless includeArchived is true. Service quota counts only live issues. Action counts include archived issues via includeArchived: true. This creates a real discrepancy. If archived issues fill the action limit the service never runs.

The action is the stricter gate. The service quota is redundant and weaker for archived issues. Rate limits are not on this path. Webhook delivery enqueues a row and drains later. Search upserts search_documents. Usage increments issuesUsed. Activity inserts events. The form resets on success via useFormAction without navigation.

content.text:
A signed-in member submits the new-issue form on `src/app/(dashboard)/[orgSlug]/projects/[projectSlug]/issues/new/page.tsx`. That page renders `IssueForm` from `src/components/domain/issue/issue-form.tsx` with `onSubmit={createIssueAction}`. The form is a client component. `useForm` validates with `zodResolver(createIssueSchema)` from `src/schemas/issue.ts`, then `useFormAction` in `src/hooks/use-form-action.ts` calls the Server Action. On `{ ok: true }` the form resets. On `{ ok: false }` it shows `result.error` through `ErrorMessage`. Nothing navigates away.

`createIssueSchema` requires branded `orgId` and `projectId`, a title of 3–200 characters, an optional description up to 20,000 characters, `status` (default `"backlog"`), `priority` (default `"none"`), nullable `assigneeId`, `parentId`, `estimate` (0–100), and `dueAt`, plus at most 20 `labelIds`.

## The Server Action

`createIssueAction` in `src/actions/issues/create-issue.ts` is a `"use server"` function. It does not implement the gates itself. It returns `run(raw)`, and `run` is `withAction` from `src/actions/_lib/with-action.ts` bound to `createIssueSchema`.

`withAction` does this, in order:

1. `schema.safeParse(raw)`. A Zod failure becomes `stamp(toActionResult(parsed.error))` from `src/lib/errors.ts`: `{ ok: false, error, submittedAt }`. The handler never runs.
2. `resolveActorFor(parsed.data, true)`. The payload has `orgId` and no `orgSlug`, so this calls `requireActorFor(orgId)` in `src/lib/actor.ts`. That reads the session cookie through `getSessionPrincipal()` in `src/lib/session.ts` (`cookies()` → `resolveSession`). No cookie, an unknown token, or an expired session throws `UnauthorizedError`. A missing `activeOrgId` throws `NoMembershipError`. Otherwise it loads the org with `findOrgById`, resolves the membership with `resolveActorForOrg(principal, org.slug)`, and calls `assertOrgScope(actor, orgId)` in `src/lib/tenant.ts` so the actor’s org matches the id in the form. The result is an `Actor`.
3. The handler runs. Any throw is caught and returned as `stamp(toActionResult(error))`. `ForbiddenActionError` and `PlanLimitError` in `src/actions/_lib/action-errors.ts` map to `forbidden` and `plan_limit_exceeded`. Service errors such as `PermissionDeniedError`, `TenantScopeError`, `NotFoundError`, and `AlreadyArchivedError` map the same way. A successful return is stamped `{ ok: true, data, submittedAt }`.
4. After the handler resolves, `withAction` also calls `revalidateTagged(["issues"], "minutes")` because the action was registered with `{ revalidate: ["issues"], cacheProfile: "minutes" }`.

The handler itself, still in `create-issue.ts`:

1. `can(actor, "issue:create", { kind: "issue", orgId, projectId, issueId: "" as Issue["id"], authorId: actor.userId, assigneeId })` from `src/lib/permissions.ts`. `explain` checks, in order: `actor.orgId === resource.orgId` (else `denied_cross_tenant`), `actor.isPlatformStaff` (else `granted_by_staff`), then `ROLE_MATRIX`. `"issue:create"` requires role `"member"`. Viewers fail with `denied_by_role`. Ownership escalation does not cover `issue:create`. A false result throws `ForbiddenActionError("issue:create")`.
2. `assertProjectHasRoom(actor, input)`. `getOrganizationSummary` in `src/server/services/organization-service.ts` checks `assertOrgScope` and `assertCan(actor, "org:read", …)`, then loads the org. `getPlanLimits(summary.organization.plan)` in `src/config/plan-limits.ts` supplies `issuesPerProject` (100 on free, higher on paid plans, `Infinity` where unlimited). `listIssues(actor, { orgId, projectId, limit: 1, includeArchived: true })` counts every issue in the project, archived rows included, because `issueFilters` in `src/server/repositories/issue-repository.ts` drops the `archived_at IS NULL` predicate when `includeArchived` is true. `listIssues` on the service also requires `issue:read` on the org. If `existing.total >= limits.issuesPerProject`, it throws `PlanLimitError("issuesPerProject", limit, total)`.
3. `createIssue(actor, input)` in `src/server/services/issue-service.ts`.
4. `revalidateTagged([orgTag(orgId), projectTag(projectId), issueTag(issue.id)], CACHE_PROFILES.minutes)` in `src/lib/cache.ts`, which calls Next’s `revalidateTag` for `org:…`, `project:…`, and `issue:…`.

The new-issue page already hid the form with the same `can` check and the same archived-inclusive quota (`notFound()` or the “This project is full” panel). Submit checks them again.

## Service gates, then the row

`createIssue` runs four more gates before it writes:

1. `assertOrgScope(actor, input.orgId)`.
2. `projectRepo.findProjectById`. `requireFound` throws `NotFoundError` if the project is missing. `assertNotArchived("Project", project.id, project)` in `src/lib/soft-delete.ts` throws `AlreadyArchivedError` if `archivedAt` is set.
3. `assertCan(actor, "issue:create", projectResource(project))`. This is the same `can` decision, now against a real project resource (`orgId`, `projectId`, `visibility`, `leadId`) from `projectResource` in `src/server/services/_support.ts`. Failure throws `PermissionDeniedError`.
4. Load the org again and `issueRepo.countIssues(orgId, projectId)`. The default archive scope keeps only live rows (`livePredicate` / `archived_at IS NULL`). `wouldExceedLimit(org.plan, "issuesPerProject", used)` throws a plain `Error` when `used + 1` is above the plan ceiling. The action’s archived-inclusive count is the stricter of the two, so this second check only fires when live issues alone already fill the quota.

Then:

- `nextIssueNumber` takes `max(issues.number)` for that org and project, archived rows included, and adds 1.
- `insertIssue(input, actor.userId, number)` inserts into the `issues` table defined in `src/server/db/schema/issues.ts`: a new id, `org_id`, `project_id`, `number`, title, description, status, priority, `author_id` set to the actor, assignee, parent, estimate, due date, `started_at` and `completed_at` left null, and `created_at` / `updated_at` set to now. The unique index is `(project_id, number)`.
- If `labelIds` is non-empty, it inserts those pairs into `issue_labels` (`org_id`, `issue_id`, `label_id`).
- It returns the `Issue` from `toIssue`.

`createIssue` does not emit `issue.assigned`, even when `assigneeId` is set. The notification fan-out in `src/server/services/notification-service.ts` listens for `issue.assigned`, `issue.overdue`, `comment.created`, and `member.joined`, so creating an issue does not notify the assignee.

## What runs because of the write

After the insert, `createIssue` awaits `emit("issue.created", …)` from `src/lib/event-bus.ts`. The payload is `actorEnvelope(actor)` plus `issueId`, `projectId`, `title`, `assigneeId`, and `priority` (`TaskflowEventMap["issue.created"]` in `src/types/event.ts`). `emit` runs every subscriber with `Promise.allSettled`. A handler that throws is reported and does not fail the action or the other handlers.

Those subscribers are attached once per process by `registerEventHandlers()` in `src/server/services/event-registry.ts` (from `src/instrumentation.ts`):

- `registerActivityListeners` in `src/server/services/activity-service.ts` calls `record`, which inserts an activity row through `activityRepo.insertActivity`: action `"issue.created"`, the actor, subject kind `"issue"`, the new issue id, project id, summary `Created issue "<title>"`, and metadata `{ priority }`.
- `registerSearchListeners` in `src/server/services/search-service.ts` re-reads the issue with `findIssueById` and, if it is still there, `indexIssue` upserts a search document whose body is the title and description.
- `registerUsageListeners` in `src/server/services/usage-service.ts` calls `usageRepo.incrementUsage(orgId, { issuesUsed: 1 })`.
- `registerWebhookListeners` in `src/server/services/webhook-service.ts` calls `enqueueForOrg`. For each enabled endpoint whose `eventTypes` include `"issue.created"`, `webhookRepo.enqueueDelivery` writes a delivery row. The payload is `JSON.stringify` of the event. Delivery itself is later, when the job drains those rows.

The action then revalidates the org, project, and issue cache tags, `withAction` revalidates the static `"issues"` tag, and the client receives the stamped `Issue` and clears the form.
